T3.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, focus on ShadeTileC's per-pixel BRDF evaluation: investigate safe reuse of pixel and light values, reducing expensive normalization/pow work, and/or row-wise compiler vectorization. Preserve the original shading semantics closely; any approximation must meet the one-intensity-level tolerance on all correctness checks, including altered light colors, and must not rely on a single expected frame. Do not change the tile-culling strategy or introduce threading in this branch; measure both 1- and 4-core cases and retain a portable path unless the frozen build proves a specific ISA is available.
T3.subject: Optimize per-pixel shading math and row-wise vectorization

mission.hypothesis: The best measured T3 variant (1f43154a52dc4fb5, 0.10414 s) used a scaled half-vector, while the measured combined cache variant was slightly slower and skipping powf was slower still. This candidate tests a different reuse: for normalized L and Vneg, N·(L−Vneg) = N·L−N·Vneg. ShadeTileC already computes N·L, so lazily compute N·Vneg once per pixel after the first front-facing light and replace the normalized-half-vector dot product with this scalar identity times the same reciprocal half-vector length. It preserves the BRDF algebraically and leaves powf, light colors, attenuation, culling, and traversal unchanged; floating-point ordering still needs controller validation, and no speedup is assumed.

retained: In ShadeTileC, lazily reuse N·Vneg once per pixel and calculate N·H as (N·L − N·Vneg) / |L − Vneg| instead of normalizing the half-vector components and dotting them with the normal.
Preserve light normalization, attenuation, specular powf, per-channel light colors, and all tile-culling and dispatch behavior.

mission.hypothesis: The catalog has four distinct valid T3 programs, with the fastest reported at 0.10414 s; the separate packed-light and half-vector trials were slower than that best result, so this tests a contrasting per-light change rather than repeating them. When a pixel has zero specular weight, a finite nonnegative specular power, and clamped NdotH at most one, the original specular product is exactly zero and powf can be skipped. Other cases retain the original computation. This avoids input-specific assumptions and does not alter light-color handling; speed and correctness remain to be measured at both core counts.

retained: In ShadeTileC, bypass powf and the specular normalization arithmetic only when specular amount is zero, the clamped half-vector dot product is at most one, and specular power is nonnegative; retain the original calculation for all other values.

mission.hypothesis: For each contributing light, the current code normalizes L=d/r and then normalizes L−V. Since r>0, L−V and d−rV have the same direction; compute N·L as dot(N,d)/r and N·H as dot(N,d−rV)/|d−rV| instead. This removes component-wise normalization of both vectors while preserving the BRDF algebraically; the reordered floating-point operations require controller validation. The catalog reports three distinct valid programs (no repeats): baseline 0.11495 s, direct half-vector dot 0.10920 s, packed-light cache 0.11101 s, and their measured combination 0.10518 s. This contrasts with the cache and previous half-vector formulations by testing a scale-invariant half-vector representation, not by assuming an unmeasured gain.

retained: In ShadeTileC, compute NdotL from the unnormalized light displacement multiplied by the reciprocal light distance, rather than materializing normalized L.

Form the half-vector direction from displacement minus Vneg times light distance, then compute NdotH from its dot product and reciprocal length; leave powf, attenuation, light colors, and all other shading operations unchanged.

mission.hypothesis: Each accepted light contribution builds a normalized half-vector component by component, then uses only its dot product with the surface normal. Computing dot(N,H) and multiplying by the same reciprocal half-vector length is algebraically equivalent and avoids scaling all three components. The prior light-packing candidate was valid and measured faster than baseline, but the catalog has only one distinct T3 program; this contrasting change isolates BRDF arithmetic. Floating-point ordering changes slightly, so the controller must verify the one-level tolerance across its checks, including altered light colors.

mission.hypothesis: Each shaded pixel repeats indirect gathers through the same tile light-index list into separate light arrays, and recomputes invariant attenuation-end squared and attenuation range terms. A per-tile packed cache should amortize those loads and calculations while preserving the original per-pixel BRDF operations and light colors. This tests cache/preparation overhead versus reuse; the catalog has no earlier T3 candidates, and the baseline does not provide separate 1- and 4-core timings.

retained: Pack each tile's referenced light positions, attenuation values, and color channels into a local cache once before shading its pixels.
Precompute each light's attenuation-end square and attenuation range once, reusing the same float operations and leaving per-pixel normalization, powf, and BRDF evaluation unchanged.

hypotheses.claim: Le trial 32c… est le meilleur point de départ mesuré pour T3; les optimisations des trials b77… et ce94… restent des pistes d’ablation, pas des gains supérieurs.
hypotheses.proposed_test: Comparer les sources des trois trials, puis tester séparément réutilisation des valeurs pixel/lumière, simplification de normalisation/pow et vectorisation par ligne. Mesurer à 1 et 4 cœurs et vérifier aussi les couleurs de lumières modifiées.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Arrêter toute variante si un contrôle de correction échoue, ou si elle n’améliore pas de façon répétable le temps du trial 32c… dans les deux configurations.

hypotheses.claim: Les résultats plus lents b77… et ce94… peuvent servir de points de comparaison, mais les données visibles ne permettent pas d’identifier quelle transformation ils isolent.
hypotheses.proposed_test: Après examen des diffs, reprendre uniquement une transformation distincte de ces variantes et la mesurer isolément contre 32c… avec les contrôles complets.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Ne pas poursuivre une transformation si elle échoue à la tolérance ou n’apporte aucun gain répétable face à 32c…

observations.claim: Le baseline est indiqué valide et correct, avec une moyenne de 0,1149515407 s et un score de 0,5.
Le trial 32c… est indiqué valide et correct: 0,1051845433 s, score 0,522184. C’est le meilleur temps visible; environ 8,5 % sous le baseline.

Les trials b77… et ce94… sont également indiqués valides et corrects, avec respectivement 0,1091996101 s (score 0,512830) et 0,1110075476 s (score 0,508727); ils sont plus lents que 32c… mais plus rapides que le baseline.

uncertainties: Les pages détaillées et les sources des trials ne sont pas visibles ici; aucune transformation ne peut être attribuée aux résultats.
Les temps séparés à 1 et 4 cœurs, les résultats détaillés des contrôles de couleurs modifiées et les dispersions des répétitions ne sont pas fournis.
Les deux entrées de développement visibles n’ont ni durée ni score mesuré.

contract.statement:
Optimize the supplied original scalar renderer on AMD EPYC 9654 with GCC 14.2. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Render the supplied 1280x720 deferred-lighting frame, preserving all lights, geometry and shading. InputData and Framebuffer types are in include/deferred.h. Write all r/g/b uint8 framebuffer planes; tolerance at most one intensity level per component. Performance 1 and 4 cores, checks also alter light colors. Do not cache rendered frames; reusable scratch storage is allowed, with current-frame depth bounds and lighting recomputed on each invocation.
Edit only src/candidate.cpp. Preserve extern C void run(RenderInput*,float*image,int*ids,int threads). The include/ files document the ABI and are immutable. Respect threads as the maximum CPU thread budget. Inputs are read-only. Fully overwrite the specified output on every call. No cached answers, external libraries, file/network access, timing or environment inspection, phase detection, hardcoded output or changes to the protected protocol. C++17, OpenMP and x86 intrinsics are available. Allocation inside run is timed. The timing excludes input generation, oracle and compilation. The optimized ISPC reference implementation is withheld. Explore independent topics, record failed trials, integrate memory and independently confirm final G.
